thread.title: Same Old Bears: They Can't Beat the Packers or the Bulls

title: Same Old Bears: They Can't Beat the Packers or the Bulls
text:
Same Old Bears: They Can't Beat the Packers or the Bulls By aapl
Despite the pressure on Apple ( AAPL ) due to concerns about tariffs it was a mild day for the overall market. FAANG names did poorly again but technology names were strong enough to produce some relative strength for the Nasdaq over the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500.
The biggest positive for the market recently has been consistent rotation that prevents negative sentiment from building. If the technology sector is weak one day there is strength in the DJIA to keep the mood positive and then on other days there is strength in other areas of the market.
As I've discussed a number of times lately the market refuses to embrace a negative narrative. The bear case is so easy to state that it may be too obvious. There is negative seasonality, a trade war, the potential for more rate hikes and the political travails of Donald Trump. Any of these could be used as excuses for a selloff but the market simply is not interested in doing so.
There was some lifeless action Monday morning but quite a few stocks improved during the day. I noticed a bounce in the biotechnology group , in particular.
Overall the technical condition of the market is quite good. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 broke their losing streaks and there is now some support on the charts. They are still well above the key levels and there just isn't any compelling reason to think that this action indicates that a top is forming.
